author: Ifmyante
text:
Oh that really sucks!

Sorry for your loss on a great winner......

A drop in the value of a currency is made to scare and subdue the
people. It's an excuse to stop investment in infrastructure and
temporarily stop handing out loans (not that I agree with debt in any
way!)

It should also create a drop in the value of the corporations. But in this case, it didn't.

So, the people will be made to suffer, while the corporations are being propped up.

Now, if our masters didn't already own everything, they'd have crashed
the London and German stock markets, so they could buy up all the
companies at pennies on the pound. But it seems that was done a long
time ago!

So, with this move, the English people can be punished for their
democracy, and frightened into accepting a recount favouring a remain
vote, or a re-vote in the near future

Remaining is easier for our masters than exiting. But destroying the
quality of life of the English people would make an example of them, and
 scare everybody else out of thinking of leaving.

Let's see how long it takes for the NHS and education system to come under threat

author: Jambowlyai
text:
Hey IF,

A few quick Qs about the course.

How many modules will there be?

Do you think the first module will be more than enough to get somebody on the right path?

Do you foresee there being a time limit on how long the Lite course modules remains available?

For somebody with limited funds which module would you recommend?

Thanks!

author: Ifmyante
text:
Well, I've made two modules, and there will soon be a subscription service where I send out the levels I'm interested in.

The first module will be on the Quasimodo and the Diamond, which, as all the old hands know, are enough to make a living off.

Yes, I don't see this going on indefinitely. There'll have to be a cap
on how many people use this stuff, or it will become obsolete.

For someone with limited funds, I'd recommend pulling sleeves up and making the free education work for you.

Putting yourself under financial pressure to take these courses is setting yourself up to fail.

author: Ifmyante
text:
This is such an important point, it needs its own post:

If you can't afford to lose the cost of a trading course, you absolutely must not invest in the trading course!

When I used to play poker in poker rooms, I hated to see young couples
come in, with their last €100 in the World, hoping to turn it into
enough to live on.

They always left ten minutes later, broken

author: Ifmyante
text:
Hiya

1) I'm not sure I understand you

2) I have no idea. I've removed myself from making financial decisions, except to insist nothing must be too expensive.

3) It's how I used to trade. Sometimes I'd make 50% per month, but more
often I'd make 200 - 400% (I'd never recommend anybody spend as long as I
 did in front of the charts!).

So, let's say one does half as well as my worst month. What capital do you need to make 25% profit cover your expenses?

The first reason I left the J16 method was that one needed a massive
account to be able to live off the minuscule profits. I wanted to be
able to make really worthwhile returns, and that's what I want for you
guys too.

Now, I'm off swimming with the kids. Have a great day

text:
boby...post 2007

Ifmyante wrote: It's very simple stuff.

One module will be step by step instructions on trading the Quasimodo and Diamond

Another will be on trading Compression

Both of these will have exact instructions on money management, entry, stop and target placement

Another one in development is trading psychology.

Each will be completed in one day, but will need to be re-studied in
one's own time, many dozens of times (instinct doesn't come from being
told something once).

I think (at least, I sincerely hope!) that anybody who's meant to be a
trader will be able to make good profits from these courses.

Oh. How does it differ from the Academy?

Well,where the academy teaches a complete understanding of price, these
courses will just be simple treading systems which need an awful lot
less understanding
